items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Paul Campbell was a little fellow, and Lester used to call him 'Ripty Gipty'... I'd seen him do it many a time

ctx.x: They were names of endearment, you know, like, well, you know about Lady Day; that's been stated many times that he gave her that name. I don't know, you know?

But like we had a little trumpet player, you know -- some little guys act like little men, and they become really to other guys, they would say, "He's a cute little man, isn't he?" Well, Paul Campbell was a little fellow, and Lester used to call him "Ripty Gipty", so you know, I guess he would come up with many things that way.

About his playing, I think that -- I'm only sorry that he really didn't get a chance to express himself. More than he did. I'll tell you what he would do at sessions. He loved to play jam sessions, and loved to not know the tune. You know? And during the sessions, a lot of times, if you were playing a tune, the instrumentalist -- the soloist -- didn't know, well, it was fashionable for the pianist to turn around and say, E flat, 7th, you know, D flat, C Major -- he wouldn't want that. If he didn't know the tune,…
